input.quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
input.rationale: Nova Scotia law and courts are outside our accepted list (New York preferred; Delaware, California or England and Wales as fallback), so the clause fails both positions. It is not walk-away territory — venue is non-exclusive and Nova Scotia is our own home province rather than Garman's (Saskatchewan) — so this is a low-heat point: we have proposed New York and will accept any name on the accepted list.

input.quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
input.rationale: Section 20(d) (reinforced by the Section 3(c) transfer bar) is a blanket consent requirement with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out for Sparkling and no reasonableness standard, which is walk-away territory under our playbook. We added the affiliate/successor carve-out for Sparkling, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard for other assignments, and confirmed a change of control of Sparkling gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right.

input.quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
input.rationale: Garman owning its base Software is acceptable, but Section 13 also vests ownership of the Modifications and Improvements — including the Schedule "D" Modifications built for us — in Garman, while the only licence back (Section 2) is a non-transferable, non-exclusive right to use the "Software" at Authorized Locations with no right to modify or sublicense, and the Agreement is silent on ownership of Sparkling's data (including data converted under Section 4). That falls short of the fallback licence-back. We added a Sparkling data-ownership sentence and a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence covering Improvements and Modifications.

input.quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
input.rationale: The grant expressly covers Sparkling's affiliated companies (no notice condition), is not revocable at Garman's discretion — it runs perpetually while fees are paid and can only fall away on termination under Section 17 — and the escrow licence in Section 16(b) is perpetual and fully paid. This meets the fallback. We note that contractors acting on our behalf are not named and the licence is non-transferable; transferability to a successor is addressed in our assignment redline rather than flagged twice here.
